blocks.text: The Martyrdom of Hadhrat Baraa bin Maalik (RA) in Persia

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "I came to (my brother) Baraa bin Maalik (RA) while he was singing something. I said, 'Allaah has given you something (the Qur'aan) that is better (than the poems you sing).' He replied, 'Do you fear that I shall die on my bed? Never! I swear by Allaah that He will never deprive me (of martyrdom). I have already killed a hundred Kuffaar apart from those whom I killed with the help of others.'" [^1]

Another narration states that when the Muslims retreated during the Battle of Aqaba in Persia, Hadhrat Baraa bin Maalik (RA) stood up and mounted his horse as another person guided it from behind. He then said to his companions, "Terrible is the habit that you people have made the enemy accustomed to (by being repeatedly defeated)!" He then led the attack against the enemy and Allaah gave victory to the Muslims. It was on that day that Hadhrat Baraa (RA) was martyred. [^2]
The Thoughts of Hadhrat Umar (RA) when Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) Passed Away without being Martyred

Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah bin Utba (RA) says that the news reached him that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "When Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) died naturally without being martyred, his status dropped in my eyes. I said to myself, 'Look at this man who was extremely abstinent from the world and then passed away without being martyred!' Uthmaan (RA) stayed in this position in my estimation until Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away. I then said, 'Shame on me! Even the best of people pass away naturally.' When Abu Bakr (RA) passed away naturally, I said, 'Shame on me! Even the best of us pass away naturally.' The status of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) was then restored to the position it previously enjoyed in my sight." [^3]
blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Abdullaah bin Utba (RA)

blocks.text: The Bravery of Hadhrat Abu Bakr Siddeeq (RA)

Hadhrat Ali (RA) once asked, "O people! Who is the bravest person?" "You are, O Ameerul Mu'mineen," the people submitted. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then said, "Although I have defeated everyone who has confronted me, I want you people to tell me who is the bravest person."
